quick.summary: How to tell if an uptick in numbers is real or just random noise.
quick.takeaway: A real signal is a jump much larger than the normal daily bounce.

beats.line: The new button got ten more clicks. Why are we not celebrating?
Imagine a road sign with five raindrops on it.
Okay. It is a slightly wet sign.
Next minute, it has fifteen raindrops. Is it a storm?
No. It is just a few more drops of water.
Right. Ten more clicks out of thousands is just drops.
We call this statistical noise.
Can I just say random chance?
Random chance works perfectly.
You need enough drops to prove it is really raining.
But how do we know when the rain is real?
To spot real rain, you look at the whole sky.
We are back to my ten extra clicks now.
Right. We expect clicks to bounce around every single day.
You only celebrate when the jump is bigger than the bounce.
So if it usually jumps by fifty, ten means nothing.
Exactly. Ten is inside your normal daily bounce.
When a jump is bigger than normal, it is a signal.
And if it jumps by two hundred clicks?
That is a signal worth throwing a party for.
I will save the balloons for a real storm then.
Keep your eyes on the sky.

quiz.question: When checking daily metrics, what indicates a true shift in performance?
options: A jump that exceeds the normal daily bounce.
Any positive movement two days in a row.
A drop followed by an immediate rise.
quiz.explanation: Metrics always wiggle a little bit. Only a jump much larger than the normal daily wiggle tells you something real happened.

quiz.question: If your metric usually moves by forty a day, an increase of ten could easily be random chance.
quiz.explanation: Ten is well within the usual daily movement of forty, so on its own it is not a signal.
